A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CGM research. Their text, tables, equations, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CGM evaluations on issue fixing and code completion, plus component ablations, backbone comparisons, and computational measurements in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix C. Results retained from v1 still qualify as original results of the work.

M1.justification: The code-graph construction, CodeT5+ encoder, adapter, graph-aware attention, reconstruction pre-training, noisy fine-tuning, and four-module Graph RAG procedure remain unchanged. The redrawn graph illustration does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Python/Java training coverage and evaluate SWE-bench Lite, SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench-java Verified, CrossCodeEval, and ComplexCodeEval. The appendix case studies and selected evaluation samples are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–4 and the appendix comparisons. Table 1 identifies Lingxi's previously unspecified backbone as Claude-3.5-Sonnet; this supplies information about the retained comparator rather than establishing a different evaluated method.

E3.justification: The reported training budgets, model configurations, evaluation metrics, retrieval procedures, and sample selections remain unchanged. This includes the 300/500/91 issue benchmarks and 100 ComplexCodeEval samples per language with middle-line completion.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same retrieval-recall analysis, cost measurements, Graph RAG ablations, semantic/structural integration ablations, reconstruction ablation, and backbone comparisons. Appendices A and D retain the same illustrative cases and graph-versus-no-graph patch comparison.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: The benchmark, ablation, recall, and computational results match. For example, Tables 1–2 retain 43.00% on SWE-bench Lite, 50.40% on Verified, and 14.29% on Java Verified. v4 Figure 1 redisplays existing Table 1 results without adding outcomes.

T1.justification: The directed-graph definition and edit-similarity formula in Appendix C.6.3 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about graph-integrated open-source LLMs, agentless repository-level engineering, and the 43.00% SWE-bench Lite result. The new chart repeats an existing ranking claim.

C2.justification: The explanations of graph integration, component effectiveness, Java retrieval difficulty, and backbone-dependent performance are retained. Appendix E preserves the same limitation to Python/Java and the need to reconsider graph construction for other programming paradigms.

D1.justification: v4 replaces the first-page anonymous code link with a named GitHub repository link and adds a Hugging Face model-checkpoint link. Table 1 also specifies Lingxi's backbone as Claude-3.5-Sonnet-20241022 instead of NA. Training details, hardware, hyperparameters, and all four appendix prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 72 cited works and substantive positioning against graph-based, agent-based, and agentless approaches are retained. Alphabetizing the bibliography and switching to author-year citations are presentation changes.

P1.justification: v4 revises front matter, shortens affiliation text, removes the keywords line, and changes citation style and running-header wording. The scientific prose and ordering of Sections 1–6 and Appendices A–F remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 substantially redesigns the presentation: it adds a first-page results chart, redraws the horizontal colored repository graph as a vertical monochrome diagram, and changes typography, margins, branded headers, table highlighting, and figure placement throughout. Existing results are redisplayed rather than expanded.

improvement.justification: v4 offers clearer resource-access information through named code and model-checkpoint links, clarifies Lingxi's backbone, and provides a convenient visual overview of existing results in Figure 1. These are useful but limited improvements: the scientific methods, empirical support, interpretations, and limitations remain unchanged.
